name: Chena Hot Springs Resort
description: Alaska's only full-service hot spring resort, located 56 miles northeast of Fairbanks. Features indoor and outdoor mineral pools, an ice museum, lodging, and aurora viewing in winter.
best_time: Weekday mornings for fewer crowds. Winter nights for northern lights.
insider_tips: The outdoor rock lake is the highlight. Stay overnight for aurora viewing from the hot springs.
wikipedia_summary: Chena Hot Springs is an unincorporated community and hot spring resort in the Fairbanks North Star Borough, Alaska, United States, 56.5 miles (90.9 km) northeast of Fairbanks near the Chena River State Recreation Area. The resort makes use of the first low-temperature binary geothermal power plant built in Alaska, and is working on several alternative energy projects, including production and use of hydrogen and vegetable oil for fuel. The resort is conducting collaborative experiments in greenhouse production of vegetables with the University of Alaska Fairbanks Agricultural and Forestry Experiment Station.

name: Alyeska Nordic Spa
description: Alaska's first Nordic spa, set in the Chugach Mountains at Alyeska Resort in Girdwood. Features 50,000 sq ft of indoor-outdoor hydrotherapy pools, cold plunges, saunas, and steam rooms.
best_time: Weekday afternoons for a quieter experience.
insider_tips: Book in advance. Stay at Alyeska Resort for spa package deals.
wikipedia_summary: Alyeska Resort is a ski resort in the Girdwood area of Anchorage, Alaska, approximately 30 miles (48 km) from downtown Anchorage. Mount Alyeska is part of the Chugach mountain range and the Alyeska Resort is the largest ski area in the state. It includes the mountaintop Mt. Alyeska Roundhouse, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

name: Pilgrim Hot Springs
description: A historic geothermal oasis on the Seward Peninsula near Nome. Surrounded by cottonwood trees and tundra, the springs were once a Catholic mission and orphanage. Road accessible in summer only.
best_time: Summer months when the road is passable.
insider_tips: The road from Nome requires a high-clearance vehicle. Check road conditions before heading out.
wikipedia_summary: Pilgrim Hot Springs is a ghost town in the interior of the Seward Peninsula of northwestern Arctic Alaska. Also known as Kruzgamepa, Kruzgamepa Springs and Unaatuq. It is located on the southeast bank of the Kruzgamepa River, about 8 miles (13 km) south of milepost 65 of the Kougarok Road, on the traditional lands of the Kauweramiut, also known as the People of Kauwerak, also known as people of the Village of Mary's Igloo and their descendants.

name: Kanuti Hot Springs
description: Remote geothermal springs within the Kanuti National Wildlife Refuge in Alaska's Interior. Best accessed in warmer months via a long hike or ski trip. No facilities.
best_time: Summer for easier access. Winter for ski-in adventure.
wikipedia_summary: Kanuti Hot Springs is a geothermal spring in an area of critical environmental concern in the Kanuti National Wildlife Refuge, Alaska, 15 miles north of the Arctic Circle.

name: Baranof Warm Springs
description: A small community on Baranof Island in Southeast Alaska, accessible only by boat or floatplane. Features natural hot springs with a bathhouse and a picturesque lake setting. No roads or ferry service.
best_time: Summer for boat access. Not accessible in winter.
insider_tips: The Baranof Cross-Island Trail from Sitka ends here. Bring all supplies.
wikipedia_summary: Baranof Warm Springs is a small, primarily seasonally-occupied community located in the city and borough of Sitka, Alaska, on the eastern side of Baranof Island, from which it likely derives its name, in the Alexander Archipelago. It is occasionally referred to simply as Baranof. Baranof Warm Springs is located at 57°05′22″N 134°49′59″W.

name: Tenakee Hot Springs
description: A historic bathhouse fed by natural hot springs in the tiny town of Tenakee Springs on Chichagof Island. The community of about 100 residents is accessible by boat or seaplane. The bathhouse is free and open to all.
best_time: Year-round. Summer for easier boat access.
insider_tips: The bathhouse has scheduled hours posted at the entrance. Respect local customs and quiet hours.

name: Bell Island Hot Springs
description: Natural thermal springs on Bell Island in the Ketchikan Gateway Borough of Southeast Alaska. Accessible by boat from Ketchikan. Remote and undeveloped.

name: Hutlinana Hot Springs
description: A geothermal spring on the bank of Hutlinana Creek, about 150 miles northwest of Fairbanks. No road access. The 6-8 mile trail is primarily used in winter after freeze-up, via snowmachine, skis, or snowshoes.
best_time: Winter after freeze-up for trail access.
insider_tips: Trailhead is at mile 128 of the Elliott Highway. Watch for trapping equipment near the trail. A stone wall separates the hot pool from the cold creek.

name: Chief Shakes Hot Springs
description: Sulfur-rich hot springs with wooden soaking tubs in the Stikine-LeConte Wilderness near Wrangell. Accessible by boat up the Stikine River. Free, with two developed tubs and a shelter.
best_time: Year-round. Summer for easier boat access.
insider_tips: Bring your own drinking water. The tubs are first-come, first-served. Watch for bears along the river.

name: Little Melozitna Hot Springs
description: Remote thermal spring in the Denali Borough of Interior Alaska. No facilities or maintained trails. Very difficult access, primarily visited by adventurous locals.

name: Manley Hot Springs
description: A small community at the end of the Elliott Highway, about 150 miles northwest of Fairbanks. The hot springs are on private property and accessible by appointment only. The town has a rich gold rush history.
best_time: Year-round, but call ahead for an appointment.
insider_tips: Call ahead to arrange access. The road is paved most of the way but the last stretch can be rough.

name: Serpentine Hot Springs
description: Remote hot springs in the Bering Land Bridge National Preserve on the Seward Peninsula. Accessible primarily by bush plane or snowmachine. Features granite tors and Arctic tundra landscape.
best_time: Summer for bush plane access. Winter for snowmachine.
insider_tips: A backcountry permit may be required from the National Park Service. Weather can change rapidly.

name: Tolovana Hot Springs
description: Managed by BLM, these hot springs are in the Tolovana River valley north of Fairbanks. Features three cabins for overnight stays and natural soaking pools. An 8-mile trail leads to the springs.
best_time: Year-round. Winter trail access is popular with skiers and snowmachiners.
insider_tips: Cabin reservations required for overnight. Day use fee is $40/person. Trail can be challenging in shoulder seasons.

name: Circle Hot Springs
description: Historic hot spring and former resort in the Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area, 131 miles from Fairbanks via the Steese Highway. The resort is closed but the hot spring pool remains in usable condition. Rich in gold rush history and aurora viewing folklore.
best_time: Winter for northern lights. Summer for road access.
insider_tips: The resort buildings are condemned but the pool is still soakable. The site has a colorful history including ghost stories. Bring everything you need.

name: Ray River Hot Spring
description: A remote USGS-listed hot spring in the Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area of Interior Alaska. No facilities or developed access. Very rarely visited.

name: White Sulphur Springs
description: A US Forest Service recreation site on the north shore of Bertha Bay on Chichagof Island. Features a restored bathhouse with indoor and outdoor warm pools. A rustic cabin is available for rent. Named for the white sulfur deposits.
best_time: Year-round. Summer for easier boat access.
insider_tips: Reserve the Forest Service cabin in advance. Bring all supplies. Short boat ride from Pelican.

name: Goddard Hot Springs
description: Historic hot springs on the outer coast of Baranof Island, about 16 miles south of Sitka. Features two cedar bathhouses with covered stainless steel tubs fed by geothermal springs. Free public access with campsites nearby.
insider_tips: Accessible by boat or floatplane from Sitka. Tom Young Memorial Cabin available for overnight. Watch for black flies in summer.

name: Trocadero Soda Springs
description: A remote soda spring on Prince of Wales Island in Southeast Alaska. Accessible only by boat. Primitive and undeveloped, offering a true wilderness soaking experience in the Tongass National Forest.

name: Shelokum Hot Springs
description: A primitive hot spring in the Tongass National Forest near Ketchikan. Accessible via a 2.2-mile trail through dense forest. Remote and undeveloped with natural rock pools.
insider_tips: Trailhead is near Saxman, south of Ketchikan. Bring insect repellent.

name: Dalton Hot Springs
description: A roadside hot spring along the Dalton Highway in Alaska's Brooks Range. Informal and undeveloped, popular with truckers and adventurous travelers heading to the Arctic.
